title: Magnetic Quadrupole Lens and Current-Induced Quadrupolar Dynamics of Antiskyrmion
authors: Linfeng Du, Yang Liu, Peng Yan, Ying Su
abstract: We demonstrate that antiskyrmions can serve as magnetic quadrupole lenses that focus or defocus electric currents traversing them. We showcase the antiskyrmion core as a focal point where electron beams converge for specific injection directions, leading to anisotropic and nonuniform current distributions. Thus the current-induced antiskyrmion dynamics is profoundly modified by the magnetic quadrupole lensing via the spin-transfer torque. By incorporating quantum transport and micromagnetic simulations iteratively, we self-consistently capture the coupled dynamics of conduction electrons and antiskyrmions. Our results unveil a quadrupolar antiskyrmion Hall effect that is highly anisotropic with respect to the current direction and can be effectively tuned by the spin-orbit coupling. In particular, the current focusing (defocusing) dramatically enhances (suppresses) the antiskyrmion speed while simultaneously reducing its Hall angle, thereby overcoming a key challenge for antiskyrmion racetrack memories. Our work establishes the intrinsic current lensing as a powerful mechanism for manipulating topological magnetic textures and opens new avenues for antiskyrmion-based spintronic devices.
summary: This work demonstrates that antiskyrmions function as magnetic quadrupole lenses, which self-consistently modify the flow of conduction electrons passing through them. This lensing effect leads to a tunable quadrupolar antiskyrmion Hall effect, offering a powerful mechanism to control antiskyrmion motion for advanced spintronic memory applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the coupled dynamics between conduction electrons and antiskyrmions, specifically analyzing how the antiskyrmion acts as a magnetic quadrupole lens to modify current-induced dynamics.
main_result: The research reveals a quadrupolar antiskyrmion Hall effect (QASkHE) and demonstrates that current focusing/defocusing can suppress the Hall angle, which is crucial for developing racetrack memory devices.
method: The authors employed an iterative approach combining quantum transport calculations (for electron current distribution) with micromagnetic simulations (governed by the LLG equation) to self-consistently model the coupled system.
model_or_system: The system involves antiskyrmions stabilized by Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) on a lattice, coupled to conduction electrons subjected to Rashba Spin-Orbit Coupling (RSOC) and exchange coupling.
key_observables: Antiskyrmion speed, Hall angle, local current distribution, and the emergent magnetic fields ($\mathbf{B}_T$ and $\mathbf{B}_M$).
important_parameters: RSOC strength ($\lambda$), DMI strength ($D$), and lattice parameters ($A, K$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled by coupling quantum transport results into the classical LLG equation, and the analysis relies on the concept of magnetic quadrupole lensing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the analogy between optical and magnetic quadrupole lenses, showing how current injection angle dictates electron beam focusing/defocusing, and visualizing the resulting speed and Hall angle dependence on injection angle.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by defining the Hamiltonians, then uses iterative simulations to calculate the self-consistent current distribution and the resulting antiskyrmion dynamics, culminating in the identification of the QASkHE.
why_interesting: The self-consistent coupling between quantum electron transport (lensing) and classical magnetic dynamics (LLG) provides a rich, non-equilibrium many-body problem relevant to spintronics and topological matter.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Analogy between optical lenses (upper panels) and anti- skyrmion magnetic quadrupole lenses (lower panels). Focusing op- tical and magnetic quadrupole lenses are shown in (a), while their defocusing counterparts are shown in (b). The emergent magnetic quadrupole field of the antiskyrmion is represented by the alternat- ing blue and red shading regions. The incident electrons are focused at the antiskyrmion core, which serves as the focal point of the mag- netic quadrupole lens in (a).

FIG. 2. (a) Emergent magnetic field of an antiskyrmion at finite RSOC. (b)-(d) Spatial distributions of electron currents injected at θin = 0◦, 45◦, and −45◦, respectively. The white streamlines indi- cate the local electron current direction. The red dashed circles in (b)-(d) indicate the position of the antiskyrmion shown in (a). For θin = ±45◦, the electron current is focused and defocused at the an- tiskyrmion core, as shown in (c) and (d), respectively.

FIG. 3. (a) and (b) Polar plots of the antiskyrmion speed |v| and Hall angle Θ as functions of the electron current incident angle θin. The self-consistent results for finite RSOC (red dots) and zero RSOC (blue dots) are obtained by solving the LLG Eq. (6) with the current j(r) updated from the quantum transport calculations. The approx- imated results with uniform current (black dots) are obtained by di- rectly solving the LLG equation with j(r) = jin. The corresponding results from the generalized Thiele Eq. (7) are represented by lines of the same color as the dot symbols.

FIG. 4. (a) and (b) Antiskyrmion speed |v| and Hall angle Θ as functions of the RSOC strength λ for an electron current injected at θin = −45◦. (c) and (d) |v| and Θ as functions of λ for θin = 45◦. The red circles and black lines represent numerical results obtained by solving the LLG Eq. (6) and Thiele Eq. (7), respectively. In both equations, the current density j(r) is obtained from the quan- tum transport calculations.
